transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi… I guess the main reason I came in is I’ve just been feeling really worn out almost every day. It’s like, even if I get what should be a full night’s sleep, I wake up and my body still feels heavy, and my head feels like it’s dragging before the day even starts.  

I work as a cashier, so I’m on my feet and have to stay alert and talk to people, and lately when I get up for my shift it just feels harder than it should. Not like I stayed up all night or anything—more like I’m already tired before I’ve even done anything. It’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Um… I don’t know if I’d say sad, exactly. Not most of the time. I mean, I have moments where I feel kind of discouraged or just fed up because I’m so tired and it’s hard to get through the day, but it doesn’t feel like I’m walking around miserable all the time or crying or anything like that.

It’s more like… I feel drained, and then that makes me frustrated with myself, if that makes sense. Like I’ll think, “Why is this so hard?” But I wouldn’t really describe my mood as sad most days.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you typically like to do, like hobbies or spending time with friends and family, about as much as you used to?

I think… mostly, yeah? I still enjoy things when I actually get myself to do them. Like if I’m with family or watching something I like, I can still get into it and laugh or feel normal for a bit.

I guess the tricky part is sometimes I’m just tired enough that starting anything feels like effort, so I might put things off or do less than I used to. But it’s not that the things feel empty or like I don’t care about them anymore. Once I’m there, I usually still enjoy it.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Not really, no. I mean, I haven’t been tracking it closely or weighing myself every day or anything like that, but my clothes fit about the same, and I haven’t looked in the mirror and thought I’d noticeably gained or lost weight.

Maybe it goes up or down a couple pounds like normal, depending on what I’ve eaten or how the week’s been, but nothing that’s stood out to me as a real change.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or paying attention to things lately?

Yeah, I have noticed that some. It’s not like I can’t focus on anything at all, but my mind wanders when I’m trying to do something that should be pretty straightforward.

Like at work, at the register, I’ll be looking right at the screen and doing the transaction, and then I realize I’ve kind of lost the thread because I’m thinking about stuff at home or bills or whatever is hanging over me. Then I have to stop and double-check myself, or recount the drawer, or I’ll catch some small mistake before it becomes a bigger thing.

It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to be careless. I’m there, I’m looking at it, but part of my brain is somewhere else.
Have you been feeling anxious or nervous lately?

Yeah… I’d say I’ve been feeling anxious pretty often. It’s kind of like my mind doesn’t stay on one thing for very long, but not in a good way. It jumps around from worry to worry.

Like I’ll be thinking about money, and then before I’ve even finished that thought I’m thinking about the relative staying with us, and whether that’s putting stress on the house, and then I start worrying about my wife being stressed. Then I remember something I said I’d help with at church, or something I’m supposed to do, and then it turns into, “Am I falling behind? Am I letting people down?” And then at work I’ll start wondering if I’m messing something up or if people can tell I’m not fully on top of things.

So yeah, nervous is probably the right word. It’s not always one huge panic feeling or anything, it’s more like this constant background noise in my head where there’s always another thing to worry about.
Do you feel like you're able to find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I can’t enjoy things anymore. I still like the things I usually like when I actually get myself into them.

It’s more that sometimes I have a hard time fully settling into it, if that makes sense. Like if I’m watching something or doing something I normally enjoy, I might still laugh or still be interested, but part of me is kind of distracted or not completely relaxed. But I wouldn’t say the pleasure is gone, exactly.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed a big change there. It’s not like I’ve stopped caring about everything I used to enjoy.
Have you been feeling down or empty for most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I don’t think I’d put it that way. I mean, I have my moments where I feel worn out or kind of discouraged, sure, but not like I’m down or empty most of the day every day.

It’s more like… I get tense or preoccupied, and then if something goes wrong I might feel low for a bit, but it doesn’t feel like this constant sadness sitting on me all day. I can still have normal parts of the day where I’m talking with people or doing what I need to do and I don’t feel empty.

So, no, I haven’t really noticed that nearly every day.
Do you often find yourself worrying about the same things over and over?

Yeah, definitely. It’s like I’ll think I’m done worrying about something, and then five minutes later I’m right back on it again, or I’ve jumped to something connected to it.

Money is a big one, but it doesn’t stay just money. It’ll turn into, “Are we okay this month?” and then, “What if something unexpected comes up?” And then I’ll start thinking about the relative staying with us, and whether that’s making things harder at home, and then I worry my wife is carrying more stress than she’s saying. Then I’ll remember church stuff I said I’d help with, and I’ll start wondering if I’m dropping the ball there.

And at work, too… I’ll be at the register and start thinking, “Did I mess that up? Am I moving too slow? Can people tell I’m not totally focused?” It just kind of loops. It feels like my mind is always jumping from one thing to the next, but a lot of the same things keep coming back around.
Have you had periods in the past where you felt sad or empty for most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not sure… I don’t really remember having a time where it was like that, where I was sad or empty most of the day, almost every day. I mean, I’ve had rough stretches, like anyone, where I felt discouraged or stressed and maybe more quiet than usual, but I don’t think it was that kind of constant emptiness you’re asking about.

I guess I’d say if I’ve felt low before, it usually came and went with whatever was happening, not like it took over the whole day for days and days. So… no, not that I can really point to.
Do you often feel restless or have trouble sitting still?

I don’t know if I’d say trouble sitting still exactly. I mean, I’m not usually pacing around the room or anything like that. If I’m sitting, I can sit, especially if I’m supposed to be somewhere or I’m working or talking to somebody.

But I guess sometimes I notice I’m kind of shifting around, like adjusting in the chair or tapping my foot a little, and I don’t always realize I’m doing it until I catch myself. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by restless. It’s not like I feel like I’m going to jump out of my skin all the time. It’s more just… sometimes I have that keyed-up feeling and my body doesn’t feel fully relaxed.

So, yeah, maybe a little at times, but I wouldn’t say it’s one of the biggest things I’ve noticed.
Is your anxiety usually about a specific thing or is it more of a general feeling of worry that isn't focused on one particular issue?

It’s more general, I think. Like, it usually starts with something specific, but it doesn’t stay there very long. My mind kind of jumps around from one thing to the next.

I’ll be thinking about money, like whether we’re okay for the month, and then that turns into worrying about the relative staying with us and how that’s affecting the house. Then I start thinking about whether my wife is more stressed than she’s letting on. And then, almost like my brain is looking for the next thing, I’ll remember something I said I’d do for church and wonder if I’m behind on it or if I forgot something.

And work is another one. I’ll be at the register and start worrying, “Did I mess that up?” or “Am I going too slow?” or “Does it look like I don’t know what I’m doing?” So it’s not just one single thing. It’s like a bunch of things that keep rotating, and even if I settle one in my head for a minute, another one pops up.
Is your anxiety affecting your ability to do your job as a cashier or handle daily responsibilities?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I’m still doing my job, I’m showing up and getting through the shifts, but I’ve noticed I don’t feel as confident at the register as I used to. I’ll make a small mistake, or think I might have, and then I end up double-checking the cash drawer more often than I probably need to. It slows me down some, and then I get more worried that I’m holding things up or that someone’s going to notice.

With daily stuff, it’s kind of the same. I still do what I need to do, but I’ve had to pull back on some things. Like I used to volunteer at the food pantry more, and I’ve cut back on that because I just feel like I can’t keep up with everything right now. It’s not that I don’t want to help, because I do, but when I look at work and home and everything else, adding that on top starts to feel like too much. So I guess it is affecting things, just not in a way where everything has fallen apart.
Is your anxiety affecting your relationships with family or friends?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t think it’s caused any big fights or anything like that, at least not that I can point to and say, “That was because of my anxiety.” My wife probably notices when I’m quieter or when I’m kind of in my own head, but we haven’t really had some major blowup over it.

With family, I guess I may be less relaxed sometimes. Like if there’s already a lot going on at home, I can be more on edge, but I don’t know if that’s affecting the relationship exactly or just making me not as easygoing as I’d like to be. I still talk to people, still show up for things when I can.

Friends… honestly, I don’t have a huge social circle anyway, so it’s hard to measure. I haven’t noticed people pulling away from me or anything. So I’d say maybe it affects how present I feel sometimes, but I can’t say it’s seriously damaging my relationships.
Do you often find yourself lying awake at night because you're worried about things?

Yeah, most nights, honestly. I’ll be tired when I get into bed, like my body is ready to sleep, but then my mind doesn’t really shut off. I’ll start going over bills in my head, or thinking about my work schedule, or whether I’m doing enough at home, whether everyone in the house is okay… and it just kind of keeps circling.

Sometimes it’s not even one big thing. It’s like I lie there trying to settle down, and then one thought reminds me of another, and before I know it I’ve been awake longer than I meant to be. And even when I do fall asleep, it doesn’t always feel like I really rested. I wake up feeling like I never fully relaxed, like my brain was still half-working all night.
Do you feel like your anxiety is significantly impacting your ability to enjoy or participate in daily activities?

Yeah… I’d say it does, but maybe not in a huge, dramatic way. I’m still doing the things I have to do, like going to work and taking care of regular responsibilities, but I don’t feel as free or comfortable doing them as I used to.

At work, for example, when I’m at the register, if I make even a small mistake—or honestly, if I just think I might have made one—I’ll end up double-checking the cash drawer more than I probably need to. And then that takes extra time, and I start feeling like I’m slowing everything down, which makes it harder to just get through the shift normally. So I’m participating, but I’m not really relaxed while I’m doing it.

And outside of work, I’ve cut back on volunteering at the food pantry. I used to do that more, and I liked feeling useful there, but lately it just feels like one more thing I have to keep up with, and I don’t feel like I have the room for it. So I guess it has taken away from some things I used to enjoy or feel good about. Not completely, but enough that I notice it.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of your anxiety?

Yeah, somewhat. I wouldn’t say I’m hiding from everything or refusing to go places, but I do find myself pulling back from things when they feel like they’re going to add more pressure.

At work, it’s not exactly avoiding the register, because that’s my job and I still do it, but if I make a small mistake—or even think I might have—I’ll double-check the cash drawer more than I probably need to. It’s like I don’t trust myself to just move on. And then I get slower, and then I worry I’m holding things up, so it kind of becomes this whole loop.

The bigger example is volunteering at the food pantry. I used to do that more regularly, and I actually liked it. It felt good to help out and be useful. But lately I’ve cut back because it just feels like one more thing I have to keep track of, one more place I have to show up and do things right, and I don’t feel like I can keep up with everything. So I guess, yeah, I am avoiding or backing away from some activities—not completely, but enough that I notice it.
Do you feel like your anxiety is interfering with your relationships with your wife or other family members?

I’m not totally sure how much it is, honestly. I mean, I don’t think my wife would say I’ve completely changed or anything like that, and we’re not having some huge constant fights because of it. But I do think there are times where I’m probably harder to be around than I realize.

Like, if I’m already wound up about regular stuff, I can be a little distracted at home. My wife might be talking to me and I’m listening, but not really fully there, if that makes sense. And then later I’ll feel bad because I know she can tell when I’m in my head. I don’t mean to make her feel ignored or like I’m not interested.

With family in general, I don’t know… I still show up, I still care about everybody. I’m not cutting people off or anything. But sometimes I probably don’t enjoy time with them as much as I should because I’m busy thinking about what needs to get done or whether something’s going to go wrong. So I guess it interferes a little, but I wouldn’t say it’s ruining my relationships. It’s more like it puts a kind of tension in the background.
Do you find yourself having thoughts or images that keep coming back to you, even when you try to push them away?

Yeah… I think so, though it’s more like worries than pictures in my head. I don’t usually see an image or anything like that, but the thoughts definitely come back even when I’m trying to shut them down.

A lot of times I’ll tell myself, you know, just pray on it, leave it alone, let it be what it’s going to be. And I mean it when I say that to myself. I’ll really try to hand it over and move on. But once one worry gets started, it’s like it doesn’t stay as just one thing. It starts rolling into the next thing, and then the next thing after that, until I’m sitting there thinking through every bad way the day could go.

Like I might start with something small, and then before I know it I’m thinking, what if I mess this up, what if that causes a problem, what if someone gets upset, what if I can’t fix it, what if the whole day goes sideways. And I know, in the moment, that I’m probably making it bigger than it needs to be, but knowing that doesn’t always stop it. It’s like my mind wants to keep checking every possible bad outcome so I can be ready for it, even though it just wears me out more.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt sad or empty for most of the day, nearly every day, that lasted for at least two weeks?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve had something like that, at least not that clearly. I’ve definitely had days where I feel worn down or kind of discouraged, like I’m tired of being in my own head, but most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks straight? I’m not sure I’d describe it that way.

I mean, I can get low sometimes, especially when I feel like I’m not keeping up or I’m disappointing people, but it usually feels more like stress or being overwhelmed than this constant empty sadness. I still have moments where I’m okay, or where I can laugh at something with my wife, or just get through the day without feeling sad the whole time. So… no, I don’t think so. Not in the way you’re asking.

It’s like a bunch of things that keep rotating, and even if I settle one in my head for a minute, another one pops up.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's anxiety is interfering with their daily life
doctor.question: Is your anxiety affecting your ability to do your job as a cashier or handle daily responsibilities?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I've had to double-check my cash drawer more often because of small mistakes, and I've cut back on volunteering at the food pantry because I don't feel like I can keep up with everything.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether anxiety is interfering with work as a cashier and daily responsibilities, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… a little. I mean, I’m still doing my job, I’m showing up and getting through the shifts, but I’ve noticed I don’t feel as confident at the register as I used to. I’ll make a small mistake, or think I might have, and then I end up double-checking the cash drawer more often than I probably need to. It slows me down some, and then I get more worried that I’m holding things up or that someone’s going to notice.

With daily stuff, it’s kind of the same. I still do what I need to do, but I’ve had to pull back on some things. Like I used to volunteer at the food pantry more, and I’ve cut back on that because I just feel like I can’t keep up with everything right now. It’s not that I don’t want to help, because I do, but when I look at work and home and everything else, adding that on top starts to feel like too much. So I guess it is affecting things, just not in a way where everything has fallen apart.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's anxiety is currently at a level that interferes with social relationships
doctor.question: Is your anxiety affecting your relationships with family or friends?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically about relationship effects with family or friends, but the provided symptom profile does not include a relationship or social-interpersonal impairment item.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t think it’s caused any big fights or anything like that, at least not that I can point to and say, “That was because of my anxiety.” My wife probably notices when I’m quieter or when I’m kind of in my own head, but we haven’t really had some major blowup over it.

With family, I guess I may be less relaxed sometimes. Like if there’s already a lot going on at home, I can be more on edge, but I don’t know if that’s affecting the relationship exactly or just making me not as easygoing as I’d like to be. I still talk to people, still show up for things when I can.

Friends… honestly, I don’t have a huge social circle anyway, so it’s hard to measure. I haven’t noticed people pulling away from me or anything. So I’d say maybe it affects how present I feel sometimes, but I can’t say it’s seriously damaging my relationships.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's anxiety is interfering with their sleep
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself lying awake at night because you're worried about things?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Most nights I get in bed tired, but then I lie there going over bills, my work schedule, and whether everyone at home is okay, and even when I do sleep I wake up feeling like I never really settled down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about lying awake at night due to worry, which directly relates to sleep disturbance.

patient.answer:
Yeah, most nights, honestly. I’ll be tired when I get into bed, like my body is ready to sleep, but then my mind doesn’t really shut off. I’ll start going over bills in my head, or thinking about my work schedule, or whether I’m doing enough at home, whether everyone in the house is okay… and it just kind of keeps circling.

Sometimes it’s not even one big thing. It’s like I lie there trying to settle down, and then one thought reminds me of another, and before I know it I’ve been awake longer than I meant to be. And even when I do fall asleep, it doesn’t always feel like I really rested. I wake up feeling like I never fully relaxed, like my brain was still half-working all night.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's anxiety is interfering with their daily life to a significant degree
doctor.question: Do you feel like your anxiety is significantly impacting your ability to enjoy or participate in daily activities?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I've had to double-check my cash drawer more often because of small mistakes, and I've cut back on volunteering at the food pantry because I don't feel like I can keep up with everything.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether anxiety significantly impacts enjoyment or participation in daily activities, which directly concerns functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I’d say it does, but maybe not in a huge, dramatic way. I’m still doing the things I have to do, like going to work and taking care of regular responsibilities, but I don’t feel as free or comfortable doing them as I used to.

At work, for example, when I’m at the register, if I make even a small mistake—or honestly, if I just think I might have made one—I’ll end up double-checking the cash drawer more than I probably need to. And then that takes extra time, and I start feeling like I’m slowing everything down, which makes it harder to just get through the shift normally. So I’m participating, but I’m not really relaxed while I’m doing it.

And outside of work, I’ve cut back on volunteering at the food pantry. I used to do that more, and I liked feeling useful there, but lately it just feels like one more thing I have to keep up with, and I don’t feel like I have the room for it. So I guess it has taken away from some things I used to enjoy or feel good about. Not completely, but enough that I notice it.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of avoidance behaviors due to anxiety
doctor.question: Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of your anxiety?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I've had to double-check my cash drawer more often because of small mistakes, and I've cut back on volunteering at the food pantry because I don't feel like I can keep up with everything.
target_item.reason: The question asks whether anxiety leads to avoiding or cutting back on situations or activities; this is best covered by functional impairment, especially cutting back on volunteering and needing extra checks at work.

patient.answer:
Yeah, somewhat. I wouldn’t say I’m hiding from everything or refusing to go places, but I do find myself pulling back from things when they feel like they’re going to add more pressure.

At work, it’s not exactly avoiding the register, because that’s my job and I still do it, but if I make a small mistake—or even think I might have—I’ll double-check the cash drawer more than I probably need to. It’s like I don’t trust myself to just move on. And then I get slower, and then I worry I’m holding things up, so it kind of becomes this whole loop.

The bigger example is volunteering at the food pantry. I used to do that more regularly, and I actually liked it. It felt good to help out and be useful. But lately I’ve cut back because it just feels like one more thing I have to keep track of, one more place I have to show up and do things right, and I don’t feel like I can keep up with everything. So I guess, yeah, I am avoiding or backing away from some activities—not completely, but enough that I notice it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's anxiety is causing significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning
doctor.question: Do you feel like your anxiety is interfering with your relationships with your wife or other family members?

target_item.reason: The question asks specifically about anxiety interfering with relationships with his wife or family members, but the provided symptom profile does not include relationship impairment or family conflict as a covered manifestation.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how much it is, honestly. I mean, I don’t think my wife would say I’ve completely changed or anything like that, and we’re not having some huge constant fights because of it. But I do think there are times where I’m probably harder to be around than I realize.

Like, if I’m already wound up about regular stuff, I can be a little distracted at home. My wife might be talking to me and I’m listening, but not really fully there, if that makes sense. And then later I’ll feel bad because I know she can tell when I’m in my head. I don’t mean to make her feel ignored or like I’m not interested.

With family in general, I don’t know… I still show up, I still care about everybody. I’m not cutting people off or anything. But sometimes I probably don’t enjoy time with them as much as I should because I’m busy thinking about what needs to get done or whether something’s going to go wrong. So I guess it interferes a little, but I wouldn’t say it’s ruining my relationships. It’s more like it puts a kind of tension in the background.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of recurrent intrusive thoughts or images
doctor.question: Do you find yourself having thoughts or images that keep coming back to you, even when you try to push them away?

target_item.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
target_item.manifestation: I try telling myself to pray on it or just leave it alone, but once a worry starts it keeps rolling into another one until I'm thinking through every bad way the day could go.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about unwanted thoughts that keep returning despite trying to push them away, which most directly matches difficulty stopping or controlling worry.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so, though it’s more like worries than pictures in my head. I don’t usually see an image or anything like that, but the thoughts definitely come back even when I’m trying to shut them down.

A lot of times I’ll tell myself, you know, just pray on it, leave it alone, let it be what it’s going to be. And I mean it when I say that to myself. I’ll really try to hand it over and move on. But once one worry gets started, it’s like it doesn’t stay as just one thing. It starts rolling into the next thing, and then the next thing after that, until I’m sitting there thinking through every bad way the day could go.

Like I might start with something small, and then before I know it I’m thinking, what if I mess this up, what if that causes a problem, what if someone gets upset, what if I can’t fix it, what if the whole day goes sideways. And I know, in the moment, that I’m probably making it bigger than it needs to be, but knowing that doesn’t always stop it. It’s like my mind wants to keep checking every possible bad outcome so I can be ready for it, even though it just wears me out more.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of recurrent depressive episodes
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of time where you felt sad or empty for most of the day, nearly every day, that lasted for at least two weeks?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a depressive episode with sad or empty mood lasting at least two weeks, but the provided symptom profile only covers generalized anxiety symptoms, fatigue, sleep, concentration, impairment, and duration—not depressed mood.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve had something like that, at least not that clearly. I’ve definitely had days where I feel worn down or kind of discouraged, like I’m tired of being in my own head, but most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks straight? I’m not sure I’d describe it that way.

I mean, I can get low sometimes, especially when I feel like I’m not keeping up or I’m disappointing people, but it usually feels more like stress or being overwhelmed than this constant empty sadness. I still have moments where I’m okay, or where I can laugh at something with my wife, or just get through the day without feeling sad the whole time. So… no, I don’t think so. Not in the way you’re asking.
